title: CI: zig build test intermittently deadlocks on ubuntu-latest after ISS-0134 libc-linking (upstream ziglang/zig#22453, mitigated with bounded retry)
registered_by: Found while resolving ISS-0135 (#433) — PR #435's CI run stalled 25+ minutes in zig build test, blocking merge
scope: CI only (.github/workflows/ci.yml). No source code defect; ISS-0134's Environ portability fix itself is correct.
symptom: zig build test in the Build and unit tests CI job intermittently deadlocks with zero progress. Observed at 25+ minutes (twice) and 4m20s (once, with an earlier -j2-only mitigation already applied). Pattern each time: one test binary streams its result back over Zig 0.16's --listen=- build-runner protocol, then total silence -- the remaining ~85 binaries never report.
root_cause_analysis: PR #434 (ISS-0134) added .link_libc = true to the modules underlying most of the 86 b.addTest targets in build.zig, so zig build test now spawns ~86 concurrent 'zig test -lc' compile jobs that all touch the same shared libc/compiler-rt cache manifests under .zig-cache. This is the exact trigger condition for upstream ziglang/zig#22453 (open, milestone 'urgent', reported Jan 2025): a lock-ordering deadlock in std.Build.Cache.Manifest where one process holds a read lock on cache file A while wanting a write lock on file B, and another process holds the write lock on B while wanting the read lock on A. Neither process can proceed and neither exits, so the flocks are never released. This is a genuine upstream Zig bug, not a defect in this repository's code or CI config -- confirmed by cross-referencing the exact deadlock signature (concurrent -lc compilations racing on Cache.Manifest locks) against the GitHub issue. -j2 alone reduces the incidence (narrows the race window) but does not eliminate it, since the race only requires two concurrent -lc jobs, not a specific count.
resolution: Two things in .github/workflows/ci.yml's build job: (1) kept the -j2 cap (reduces race likelihood); (2) wrapped `zig build test` in a bounded retry loop (up to 3 attempts, 5 minutes each via `timeout 300`), since a killed/timed-out attempt releases its flock on process exit -- verified locally that a `timeout`-killed run always succeeds on retry against the same on-disk cache. Job-level timeout-minutes raised to 25 to give the retry loop room (3 x 5min attempts plus other steps). This is an honest mitigation for a confirmed upstream bug with no documented workaround, not a fix -- the underlying Zig lock-ordering bug is unpatched.
acceptance_criteria: zig build test completes reliably (via retry) without blocking PRs indefinitely
Root cause identified and cross-referenced against an upstream tracking issue
acceptance_criteria_status: Both criteria satisfied. Root cause confirmed against ziglang/zig#22453. Follow-through PR #438 reduced independent zig test compile units from 86 to 61 (-29%), directly shrinking the concurrent -lc job count that triggers the upstream race; verified 8/8 clean runs in a Docker container matching the original repro environment (2-core cgroup quota). Live GitHub Actions confirmation obtained: main push run 31015896263 (triggered by #438's merge) completed successfully on ubuntu-latest.
